pr_title: Add xiaomi_miio vacuum current cleaning cycle statistics sensor
pr_body:

## Proposed change

Before the refactoring done in #54990, clean time and area would
return the cleaning stats of the current cycle or the last
known cycle. During the refactoring, this has feature has been lost.

This reverts the behaviour back to before the refactoring.

issue_context.title: The vacuum doesn't update some sensors during cleaning
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The vacuum `roborock.vacuum.s5` doesn't update the `sensor.*_last_clean_area` and `sensor.*_last_clean_duration` during cleaning, only after returned to the dock. May be some sensors such is `cleaned_area` and `cleaning_time` is missing.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.10.*

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Xiaomi miio

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/xiaomi_miio/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @rytilahti, @syssi, @starkillerog, @bieniu, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`xiaomi_miio`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L604) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I can confirm this also on the `roborock.vacuum.e2`. In fact, I'm suspicious that none of the sensors have been updating properly since installing the `2021.11` release last week. For instance the vacuum runs multiple times each day, but it says the last clean start was 2 weeks ago...

I'm currently on `2021.11.3`

![Screenshot_20211115_144914](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2080205/141802067-d1a5a80d-ff39-42b5-b5bd-542d2bf116d7.png)

For some unknown reason, it seems the attributes cleaning_time and cleaned_area are no longer updated while the vacuum is working and only when a "job" is done (which is not the way it used to work before, as this would allow to know the actual job progress area and time-wise). These were actually migrated as integration sensors 'Last Clean Duration' and 'Last Clean Area', so not sure if this is a bug or a feature.

If it is a feature, it would be useful if we could get these attributes back or have 2 new separate integration sensors containing this "runtime" information.

Thanks in advance.

I also observed, that the Cleaned Area sensors are not resettet to zero, so my utility_meter isn't working any more. I was using it to let the vacuum clean for 120 m² before sending an alarm that the dust bin needs to be emptied.

Here you can see the last days before the update.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51734505/141992235-cc0a2422-82a8-477d-ba9d-68d166df5072.png)

Have you already tried to enable debug logging for the integration (`homeassistant.components.xiaomi_miio`) as well as for the backend lib (`miio`) to see if what is being shown by homeassistant is the same as what's being reported by the device (which is being shown in the logs)?

The first line is `miio` debug and the second line is `homeassistant.components.xiaomi_miio`, but the sensors doesn't updates
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43236573/143182176-a2d8661c-f3ad-4917-989c-b2e71742103d.png)
Debug log:
[home-assistant.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7593044/home-assistant.zip)

I can confirm the same behaviour. This is what is reported by xiaomi_miio integration:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10042655/144734196-2ef6d882-04b6-4b2f-8898-d1522e01ec51.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10042655/144734207-d9eb9634-351f-458d-a488-ac0d26fa9750.png)
This was the last completed scan, i.e. the vacuum has returned to its dock.
The last running scan is different:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10042655/144734228-48638e30-fab4-44c2-b3b1-0858dcc45697.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10042655/144734235-fd72cb86-163b-4a55-8f80-37b0dca17b52.png)
The last running scan results are correctly reported by miio backend library and another integration (xiaomi miiot). I am using it as a workaround for now, until this bug is resolved.
So it looks like the coordinator is updating the data, but not informing the sensors to update their state. @OGKevin any ideas?

So my investigation tells me the following: 

Based on my logs, during a vacuum run, the same  `id` is used to get the last cleaning details:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4144699814602e0c116bf801c2f8f26ba25edca6/homeassistant/components/xiaomi_miio/__init__.py#L245 
causes the following log entries:
```text
2021-12-05 20:26:15 DEBUG (SyncWorker_4) [miio.miioprotocol] 192.168.1.98:54321 >>: {'id': 522, 'method': 'get_clean_record', 'params': [1638735225]}
2021-12-05 20:26:16 DEBUG (SyncWorker_4) [miio.miioprotocol] 192.168.1.98:54321 (ts: 1970-01-01 18:13:16, id: 522) << {'id': 522, 'result': [{'begin': 1638735225, 'end': 1638735419, 'duration': 107, 'area': 1650000, 'error': 0, 'complete': 0, 'start_type': 2, 'clean_type': 3, 'finish_reason': 64, 'dust_collection_status': 0}], 'exe_time': 101}

2021-12-05 20:26:31 DEBUG (SyncWorker_3) [miio.miioprotocol] 192.168.1.98:54321 >>: {'id': 529, 'method': 'get_clean_record', 'params': [1638735225]}
2021-12-05 20:26:32 DEBUG (SyncWorker_3) [miio.miioprotocol] 192.168.1.98:54321 (ts: 1970-01-01 18:13:32, id: 529) << {'id': 529, 'result': [{'begin': 1638735225, 'end': 1638735419, 'duration': 107, 'area': 1650000, 'error': 0, 'complete': 0, 'start_type': 2, 'clean_type': 3, 'finish_reason': 64, 'dust_collection_status': 0}], 'exe_time': 101}

```

According to the code in the underlying lib:
https://github.com/rytilahti/python-miio/blob/5699aead1551cc1c54696e672ae0fdb1f23a8d06/miio/integrations/vacuum/roborock/vacuum.py#L453-L463

The current cleaning cycle is not part of `histroy.ids`, hence you only get the stats of literally "the last clean cycle"

In #54990 during the refactoring this feature got broken, due to the _way_ this data is being retrieved.  There are 2 ways to retrieve this data, where 1 way (the current way) literally gives you the last cleaned details, while the other way (https://github.com/rytilahti/python-miio/blob/5699aead1551cc1c54696e672ae0fdb1f23a8d06/miio/integrations/vacuum/roborock/vacuumcontainers.py#L148-L155) gives you the current time/area OR the last cleaned details.

So we have 2 options:
1. Revert the behaviour and use the retrieval that gives us the current cycle data OR the last cycle data
2. Add 2 new sensors named `current_cleaning_*` that only return the current cleaning data if the vacuum is cleaning, else none/unavailable

My apologies, for the inconvenience BTW :(  

@rytilahti feel free to poke me early on next time, there is no need to let these issue stay open for so long 👍🏾 I was not aware of this bug/issue 🙈.

How shall I proceed with the fix @rytilahti?

Hmm, good catch! Maybe it makes sense to revert the behavior here, as it will also reduce the number of required I/O requests by 2 per update cycle (1st request done internally by python-miio to find the most recent cleanup, and 2nd to obtain its details)? The only downside I'm seeing is that this will put some more info to the state machine, but that's also how it was earlier so I think it's a non-issue.

@OGKevin feel free to add yourself to the CODEOWNERS file, so you'll get automatically pinged on issues :-)

>  as it will also reduce the number of required I/O requests by 2 per update cycle

Not necessarily, `device.last_clean_details(),` is still needed for the `last_clean_start` and `last_clean_end` sensors. Unless we decide to drop those sensors, but I, for one, use these 😁  So i rather not.

> > as it will also reduce the number of required I/O requests by 2 per update cycle
> 
> Not necessarily, `device.last_clean_details(),` is still needed for the `last_clean_start` and `last_clean_end` sensors. Unless we decide to drop those sensors, but I, for one, use these 😁 So i rather not.

I second that, it is interesting to have both informations.

If we keep the 2 mentioned sensors, I would say option 2 is better, actually. If not, it could lead to other confusion. Where the last start time is representing the last start time in history, while the cleaning duration and area both represent the current cleaning cycle 🤔  

So having 2 new sensors names `current_cleaning_*` would clearly indicate the diff. Where one is about the current cycle and the other is one of the last cycle known in history.

I see. Then it makes no sense to try to optimize that right now, so I agree that we should go with option 2. This will also allow use cases like creating a template sensor for "% cleaned" based on the previous run :-)

review_comments: We don't want relative times in the state machine. In that case expose a timestamp from when the cleaning started.

This sensor is supposed to expose for how long the current cleaning cycle has been running for. There is another sensor that exposes the start time of the cycle. 

So these are 2 separate sensors.
The value of this sensor doesn't update just because time passes, right? It updates when the device has been used and the clean time increases. Is that correct?

So:
t1: I press start on the vacuum
t2: vacuum has been cleaning for x1 seconds
t3: coordinator update is ran, sensor is set to x1 seconds
t4: vacuum has been cleaning for x2 seconds 
t5: coordinator update is ran, sensor is set to x2 seconds
t6: vacuum finished cleaning, total clean time is x3 seconds
t7: last sensor update, sensor is set to x3 seconds

So basically, indeed, it updates during the time spent cleaning during the current clean cycle. Once the cleaning cycle is finished, this sensor will stop updating. Until another clean cycle has started, of course.

I did mention before that there is already a sensor indicating start time, but this sensor only updates once the cleaning cycle has finished as explained in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/59272#issuecomment-986297000

I think I understand the feedback better now. So @balloob feedback is to just use the start time of the current cleaning cycle and then users can use templates etc to figure out for how long the cycle has been running? 

The slight issue is that the device exposes the clean time in seconds. So the same argument can be made that user use template sensors to record when the state of the vacuum went from something to cleaning 🤔 .

Since the sensor only updates when the device is actually used, I think it's ok to have a relative time as value, but it would be better to report in minutes. Seconds is too high resolution and most likely not interesting. We do allow formatting times before storing in state machine.

Actually, this is then blocked on https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/59092 if we want to move an away from seconds. 

@rytilahti will you push that PR, so it gets merged, or do you want me to pick it up?
Or this one gets merged as seconds and then picked up in the above linked PR.
If we expect to break the value, we should close this PR and have it be included in the other PR ?
That other PR is for merely for adjusting the sensor granularity / units, so this PR here should probably just be rebased on top of that, either pre or post merge.
The PR to adjust the measurement unit was closed as the seconds as units was chosen to be the preferred format, so I suppose this PR can now proceed.
Will have a look later today or tomorrow.
